DPoint.text: Makes a point from two coordinates.

DPointInvalid.text: The "no point" value (both coordinates NaN) that stands for CDPoint() having no value, e.g. for hidden power pins.

DPointHasValue.returns: False when either coordinate is NaN

MakeXMLUnits.text: Converts internal units (0.2 mm) to the millimetres written in XML files.

UnmakeXMLUnits.text: Converts millimetres read from an XML file to internal units.

RGB.text: Builds a Windows color value (0x00BBGGRR) from red, green and blue.

EXMLException.CreateXML.text: Builds the error with the same wording as TinyCAD's CXMLException: the message, then "Error first detected on line #n".

params.ALine: the line number where it was detected

UUEnc.text: UU-encodes one 6-bit value as a printable character (the ENC macro of uuencode).

UUEncodeLine.text: UU-encodes up to 45 bytes as one text line: a length character then groups of four characters for each three bytes.

UUDec.text: Decodes one UU character to its 6-bit value (the DEC macro).

TUUDecoder.Feed.text: Feeds one character of UU-encoded text to the decoder, which collects the decoded bytes; handles the length character and the groups of four.

IsWS.text: Whether a character is C white space (space, tab, newline, vertical tab, form feed, return).

ScanDouble.text: Scans a C-style decimal floating point number from a string, as strtod would for ordinary input, and moves the position past it.
ScanDouble.returns: True if a number was found

params.Pos: 1-based position to start at; moved past the number on success

CAtoI.text: Converts text to an integer the way C's atoi does: skips white space, accepts a sign, stops at the first non-digit.
CAtoI.returns: the value (0 if there are no digits)

CAtoF.text: Converts text to a number the way C's atof does (0 when there is no number).

CHexToInt.text: Converts hexadecimal text (as used for colors in XML) to a number like C's strtoul with base 16.

CScanPoint.text: Reads "x,y" in millimetres as sscanf would and stores it in internal units; a field that does not parse leaves that coordinate untouched.
CScanPoint.returns: True if both numbers were read

FormatFixed5.text: Formats a number exactly like C's printf("%.5f") whatever the locale: the double is split into mantissa and exponent and rounded exactly (ties to even), unlike Free Pascal's Str which can round the wrong way near a boundary.

FormatPoint.text: Formats a point as "x,y" in millimetres with five decimals, as it is written in XML.

TXMLReader.Create.text: Parses an XML stream into a document and positions the reader on the first top-level element. Parse errors become EXMLException.

TXMLReader.Top.text: Index of the innermost nesting frame.

TXMLReader.CurrentElement.text: The element the reader is on; raises an error if it is not on an element.

TXMLReader.NextTag.text: Moves to the next element at the current level (the first one on the first call after IntoTag) and gives its name, like CXMLReader::nextTag.
TXMLReader.NextTag.returns: False when there are no more elements at this level

TXMLReader.IntoTag.text: Steps inside the current element so NextTag walks its children.

TXMLReader.OutOfTag.text: Steps back out to the parent level; an error if already at the top.

TXMLReader.RawAttr.text: Looks up an attribute of the current element as text.

TXMLReader.RawChildData.text: The text content of the current element.

TXMLReader.GetAttribute@string.text: Reads a text attribute; V is unchanged when the attribute is missing.

TXMLReader.GetAttribute@integer.text: Reads an integer attribute (C atoi rules); V is unchanged when it is missing.

TXMLReader.GetAttribute@double.text: Reads a number attribute (C atof rules); V is unchanged when it is missing.

TXMLReader.GetAttribute@boolean.text: Reads a Boolean attribute stored as 0 or 1; V is unchanged when it is missing.

TXMLReader.GetAttribute@tdpoint.text: Reads a point attribute written as "x,y" in millimetres, converting to internal units; V is unchanged when it is missing.

TXMLReader.GetAttributeColor.text: Reads a color attribute written as hexadecimal.

TXMLReader.GetChildData@string.text: Reads the current element's text content into V.

TXMLReader.GetChildData@integer.text: Reads the current element's text content as an integer.

TXMLReader.GetChildData@double.text: Reads the current element's text content as a number.

TXMLReader.GetChildData@boolean.text: Reads the current element's text content as a Boolean (0 or 1).

TXMLReader.GetChildData@tdpoint.text: Reads the current element's text content as an "x,y" point in millimetres, converting to internal units.

TXMLReader.GetChildDataColor.text: Reads the current element's text content as a hexadecimal color.

TXMLReader.GetChildDataUUDecode.text: Reads UU-encoded binary data from the element: a size line followed by encoded lines, as used for the symbol blobs inside .dsn files.

TXMLWriter.Create.text: Creates a writer that sends XML to a stream; tags are tracked so closing and indentation come out as in TinyCAD.

params.AOutput: the stream to write to; not owned

TXMLWriter.Destroy.text: Frees the tag stack. The output stream is not closed.

TXMLWriter.SendString.text: Writes text to the output and counts the lines written (used in error messages).

TXMLWriter.Escape.text: Escapes text for XML (& < > and quotes) so it can go in an attribute or element.

TXMLWriter.AddComment.text: Writes an XML comment on its own line.

TXMLWriter.CloseOpenTag.text: Finishes the start tag that is still open by writing ">".

TXMLWriter.AddTag#1.text: Starts an element: closes the previous start tag if needed, indents, and writes "<name"; attributes may follow until content is added or the tag is closed.

TXMLWriter.CloseTag.text: Ends the innermost open element, as "/>" when it has no content or with a closing tag otherwise.

TXMLWriter.InternalAddTag.text: Writes a complete element with text content in one step (open, content, close).

TXMLWriter.InternalAddAttribute.text: Adds an attribute to the open start tag; an error if the tag already has content or none is open.

TXMLWriter.InternalAddChildData.text: Adds text content to the open element (closing its start tag first); an error if no element is open.

TXMLWriter.AddTag#2.text: Writes a complete element whose text content is a string.

TXMLWriter.AddTag@integer.text: Writes a complete element whose content is an integer.

TXMLWriter.AddTag@double.text: Writes a complete element whose content is a number formatted like C "%.5f".

TXMLWriter.AddTag@tdpoint.text: Writes a complete element whose content is a point as "x,y" in millimetres.

TXMLWriter.AddTagUInt.text: Writes a complete element whose content is an unsigned integer.

TXMLWriter.AddTagColor.text: Writes a complete element whose content is a color as hexadecimal.

TXMLWriter.AddAttribute#2.text: Adds a text attribute to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddAttribute@integer.text: Adds an integer attribute to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddAttribute@double.text: Adds a number attribute (C "%.5f" formatting) to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddAttribute@tdpoint.text: Adds a point attribute written "x,y" in millimetres to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddAttributeUInt.text: Adds an unsigned integer attribute to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddAttributeColor.text: Adds a color attribute (hexadecimal) to the open element.

TXMLWriter.AddChildData@string.text: Adds text content to the open element (escaped).

TXMLWriter.AddChildData@integer.text: Adds an integer as the open element's content.

TXMLWriter.AddChildData@double.text: Adds a number (C "%.5f") as the open element's content.

TXMLWriter.AddChildData@tdpoint.text: Adds a point "x,y" in millimetres as the open element's content.

TXMLWriter.AddChildDataUInt.text: Adds an unsigned integer as the open element's content.

TXMLWriter.AddChildDataColor.text: Adds a color (hexadecimal) as the open element's content.

TXMLWriter.AddChildDataUUEncode.text: Adds binary data as UU-encoded text: the size, then lines of up to 45 bytes each, as TinyCAD writes symbol blobs.
